Subject: Clarification on Output Ownership and Training Rights — Vexor PO# 1173

Hi Marissa,

Attached is our redline of the Order Form and a short note from procurement. Two items need urgent clarification before we can route to legal sign-off:

1) Output ownership / productization: Our procurement team is asking that the Order Form explicitly state that Vexor retains exclusive ownership of outputs generated from Vexor-provided prompts and data, including any derivative products. Redwood's current draft reads more like a non-exclusive license.

2) Training / feedback license: We need confirmation that Redwood will not use Vexor data (prompts, inputs, outputs, telemetry) to train or improve any models used outside of the Vexor account without our explicit opt-in. Procurement also asks about an evidence path (audit logs, retention config) that shows data segregation.

We also included two pragmatic asks: an escrow mechanism for outputs if there is a dispute, and a short appendix describing what telemetry data is collected and how it is used.

Please confirm whether Redwood can:
- Add an explicit clause that outputs from Vexor-owned prompts are assigned to Vexor (or granted an exclusive license for productization), and
- Offer a configuration to opt-out of training/model-improvement for Vexor's data, with a description of the operational controls and cost/latency impact.

Attachment: Vexor_OrderForm_Redline.docx

Thanks,
Sarah Lin
Sr. Counsel, Vexor Systems

Marissa / team — reviewed the redline. High level: customer asks are reasonable but we should avoid blanket assignment of model output. Suggested pathway below (legal redline included as separate attachment).

Summary of proposed compromise (for procurement to accept):
- Output ownership: Customer receives an exclusive license to Productize outputs produced solely from Customer Content (their prompts/data) for their internal and external offerings; Redwood retains aggregated, de-identified telemetry and model-improvement rights under strict limitations.
- Training / feedback license: Default position: Redwood will not use Customer Content to train models used outside the Customer instance without explicit opt-in. We can offer an opt-in checkbox and an account-level setting. For auditability, we will provide an evidence bundle: retention configuration, sampling of audit logs (request IDs + timestamps), and a brief design doc describing data flow.
- Escrow: Recommend a narrow escrow scope limited to output snapshots for defined dispute scenarios — avoids full data escrow.

Draft clause suggestions (short form for procurement):
1) "Customer Output License": "Customer shall own or have an exclusive, perpetual, worldwide license to outputs generated solely from Customer Content. Redwood retains the right to use de-identified, aggregated telemetry for service analytics and to operate the Service, but shall not use Customer Content for model training without prior written consent."

2) "Training Opt-Out": "Customer may elect by account setting that Customer Content and Customer Output will not be used to train or improve models operated outside of Customer's dedicated environment. Redwood will honor the account-level opt-out within a standard operational window (30 days) and provide configured retention and audit logs as evidence upon reasonable request."

3) "Audit & Evidence": "Upon reasonable request and subject to a mutual NDA and customary redaction for security, Redwood will produce a compliance bundle containing retention settings, audit logs for the relevant timeframe and a short explanation of processing. Redwood may charge a one-time fee for extensive evidence pulls beyond routine reporting."

Open items / questions for product:
- Can infra reliably implement an account-level training opt-out and guarantee it within a 30-day window?
- What telemetry is considered "aggregated" vs "Customer Content"? We should map the variables.

Next steps: Rishi to confirm technical feasibility + operational window. Ben to confirm whether a one-time 'evidence pull' fee is acceptable commercially and any impact on the deal economics. I'll prepare redline text to send back to Vexor that preserves our ability to operate and avoids full assignment.

Attachment: legal-proposed-clauses.txt

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts & Commercial Counsel
Redwood Inference

Quick tech note from product/runtime team: we can support an account-level training opt-out and separate retention, but there are operational considerations to call out before we commit to contract language.

Feasibility & constraints:
- Implementation: We already have tenant isolation and per-tenant model routing for Dedicated; for Hosted accounts we'd enable a per-account flag that prevents logs/edges from flowing into the model-improvement pipeline. That is implementable and can be gated by deployment type (Hosted vs Dedicated).
- Window: Effective isolation will be achievable within a 30-day window after the flag is set for new data. Historical data already fed into any shared improvement pipeline cannot be retroactively removed from models; we should be explicit about that in language.
- Evidence: We can deliver a compliance bundle with request IDs, retention settings, and a high-level processing diagram. A full forensic export (every raw input) is expensive; recommend a one-time evidence fee for anything beyond standard reporting.
- Cost/latency: If we route Vexor traffic to a private variant or restrict model-improvement paths, there may be additional infra cost (small % increase) and slightly higher latency for some model families due to reduced caching sharing. We'd provide a commercial estimate once we know expected monthly token volumes.

Recommendation for contract language adjustments (short):
- Add explicit "no training" opt-out clause but include the historical-data carveout and the 30-day effective window.
- Specify types of telemetry that remain available (service metrics, anonymized usage) vs. Customer Content.
- Include a standard operational fee for large evidence requests and a note on potential minor latency/cost delta if isolation is required.

I'll work with infra to draft the operational appendix for the compliance bundle (what we can deliver and typical SLAs) by EOD tomorrow. If procurement wants full assignment rather than an exclusive license for Productization, we should push back — assignment has broader product/legal impact.

—Rishi
